modelDescription.name: MLB-M0 parent baseline
modelDescription.summary: Baseline MLB parent cartridge. MLB-M0 owns the daily workflow surface, publish lanes, MLB-specific scoring adapters, run manifest, closeout health gate, and the MLB-RP36 relief addendum boundary. Model-neutral sports plumbing now lives in models/shared/sports-core. Remaining pipeline files are source fetchers, warehouse commands, compatibility launchers, or offline research until a future model promotes them.
keyImprovements: Names the current MLB parent model as MLB-M0 so future changes can be compared against a stable baseline.
Keeps MLB-RP36 as a relief addendum consumed by MLB-M0 instead of treating the reliever shadow artifact as a separate parent model.
Adds a May 30 closeout gate so side predictions must flow into `mlb_side_predictions` and `mlb_side_backtests` before postmortem lessons are trusted.
Adds a cartridge-local performance index and quiet-start full-game gate so May 30 failures can affect the next slate instead of staying as notes.
Persists daily hitter platoon split snapshots so the prop model can be audited against the exact split context shown pregame.
Extracts model-neutral odds, participant, signal, structured-context, and match-factory contracts into models/shared/sports-core while MLB-M0 keeps only MLB adapters and MLB-specific scoring logic.
Moves MLB-M0 workflows and publish lanes into the cartridge while old pipeline paths remain compatibility launchers.
Adds a documented pipeline ownership boundary so data plumbing and offline research are not mistaken for missed model code.
Adds a component registry for sides, first-five, totals, props, HRs, market context, and MLB-RP36 so future work can land in the right model lane without scanning the whole cartridge.
Indexes MLB-M0 and MLB-RP36 run snapshots into shared warehouse model-run tables so performance/backtest queries no longer depend only on JSON files.
Adds registry-aware MLB lifecycle wrappers so future parent models can be scaffolded, run, snapshotted, checked, and compared without hardcoding package scripts to MLB-M0.
Adds an app adapter registry so future active parent models must register their app-facing contract instead of silently rendering through MLB-M0.
Routes legacy pipeline workflow/publish launchers and web prop-calibration access through registry-aware adapters.
Routes MLB-RP36 package scripts and refresh consumption through registry-aware component wrappers.

notes: MLB-M0 should eventually own the final MLB side, first-five, total, prop, and market-context outputs.
Pipeline internals that remain are classified as fetchers, warehouse commands, compatibility launchers, or offline research; production lane behavior should live in the cartridge.
MLB publish/export package commands enter through `models/mlb/run-cartridge.mjs --entry lane:<lane>`; `pipeline/mlb/publish/` is compatibility only.
`models/shared/sports-core` owns reusable sports contracts; `models/mlb/app-model.js` resolves the active MLB app adapter, and `web/src/lib/sports-model.js` re-exports the app composition path.
Do not promote MLB-RP36 into a standalone parent model; it should feed MLB-M0.
Before a new MLB slate, the prior day must have a results journal plus side prediction/backtest rows so lessons are based on warehouse-settled data.
Quiet-start, traffic-without-conversion, and quiet-first-five risks now suppress full-game side promotion unless another market expression is cleaner.
`MLB-M0_log.md` is the working log for warehouse/model changes that still need lane-specific proof.
Run snapshots remain the reproducibility artifact, but every snapshotted MLB-M0/MLB-RP36 run should also be indexed into the shared warehouse model-run tables.
New parent models should start from the model-iteration runbook and registry-aware wrappers, not by editing package scripts to point at a draft cartridge.
New parent models that alter app-facing match output must register in `models/mlb/app-model.js` before activation.
knownLimitations: Compatibility launchers remain under pipeline/mlb, but they are no longer part of the narrowed MLB-M0 source inventory.

modelDescription.name: TEN-T0 tennis baseline
modelDescription.summary: Baseline tennis cartridge for the Roland Garros pipeline after the May 31 value-book and derivative-lane cleanup. TEN-T0 is a reproducibility baseline, not a claim that the model is already good enough to bet blindly.
keyImprovements: Separated the active tennis model into a cartridge/run stack so future TEN-T1+ changes can be compared against a frozen TEN-T0 baseline.
Made ML, spread, match O/U, first-set O/U, set-win, and Kalshi trade-to-sell separate lanes instead of blending them into one vague confidence number.
Added postmatch settlement and backtest surfaces so model accuracy, lane hit rate, and ROI can be tracked by day.
Kept source-site predictions as context only; the cartridge prediction lanes are expected to come from warehouse features, market lines, and model gates.
